title: TERMy 用确定性规则替代 LLM，终端助手不再需要大模型
summary: TERMy 通过数据驱动有限状态机实现终端命令的确定性路由，在速度、成本和可审计性上优于 LLM，但无法处理未预定义的请求。
opening: TERMy 是一个不依赖大语言模型的终端助手，它用确定性规则替代概率生成，把自然语言命令映射到预设的终端操作。这个项目在 Hacker News 上获得 210 分，开发者 Giovanni Blu Mitolo 的动机很直接：AI 价格飙升，而低配硬件上的开源模型又不够快。TERMy 的价值不在于技术多先进，而在于它重新划定了“什么时候根本不需要 LLM”的边界。
core_experience:
TERMy 的核心体验是即时响应和完全可预测。用户输入“激活虚拟环境”这样的指令，系统通过词汇表匹配和语义映射，直接路由到对应的终端命令，整个过程在毫秒级完成。没有 token 生成、没有 API 调用、没有模型幻觉。开发者最初尝试训练小型 transformer，但在 GTX 1050 Ti 上效果不佳；后来测试 ollama 和开源模型，速度和可靠性也不达标。最终他转向 NPC-Forge 框架，用数据驱动的有限状态机（DDFSM）实现所有语义分析、意图处理和工具调用。

TERMy 的交互模式很朴素：用户输入自然语言，系统查表匹配意图，执行预设命令。对于“打开文件”“运行测试”这类高频操作，体验流畅。但一旦输入偏离模板，比如“帮我看看那个东西为什么跑不起来”，系统就会失败或返回兜底回复。这种体验像是一个训练有素的命令别名工具，而不是一个能理解上下文的助手。
why_it_works:
TERMy 有效的原因在于它把终端助手的任务域收窄到高频、结构化的命令请求。对于“激活虚拟环境”这类操作，用户意图明确、命令空间有限，确定性规则足以覆盖。相比 LLM，它不需要 GPU、不产生 token 费用、响应即时，而且行为可预测、可审计。开发者 Giovanni Blu Mitolo 在尝试训练小型 transformer 和运行开源模型后，发现两者在低配硬件上要么质量差要么速度慢，于是转向完全确定性的方案。这种约束驱动的设计让 TERMy 在特定场景下比通用 LLM 更实用。

从产品角度看，TERMy 的成功在于它没有试图解决“理解任意自然语言”这个难题，而是把问题转化为“如何高效匹配已知意图”。NPC-Forge 的静态 JSON 文件定义了词汇表、语义映射和命令模板，系统只需要做查表和路由。这种设计让响应时间从秒级降到毫秒级，同时完全消除了模型幻觉和 API 成本。对于终端用户来说，可预测性本身就是一种价值：你知道输入什么会得到什么，不会出现模型突然给出危险命令的情况。
boundaries:
TERMy 的边界非常清晰：它无法处理未在数据集中预定义的请求。遇到新表达或新任务，系统会直接失败或回退到兜底回复。语义理解依赖人工编写的词汇表和正则表达式，覆盖范围有限，维护成本随意图数量线性增长。缺乏上下文推理和组合能力，无法处理多步、条件或需要常识的任务。与 LLM 相比，自然语言输入的容错性低，用户必须使用接近模板的措辞才能被正确识别。

这些限制在终端场景下可能并不致命，因为终端命令本身就是高度结构化的。但一旦用户试图用自然语言描述一个模糊的目标，比如“清理一下系统里没用的东西”，TERMy 就无能为力了。它更像是一个命令别名工具，而不是一个能理解用户意图的助手。Hacker News 讨论中也提到，未来可能需要集成 LLM 来处理低置信度的查询，并让系统从 LLM 的成功回答中自动提取新规则。
personal_judgment:
TERMy 的价值不在于替代 LLM，而在于示范了一种“够用就好”的工程哲学。在 AI 价格飙升、模型臃肿的背景下，它提醒产品经理：很多高频、低复杂度任务根本不需要生成式模型。确定性系统在可预测性、成本和速度上具有压倒性优势，尤其适合嵌入式、离线或安全敏感的环境。但它的天花板也很明显——一旦用户需求超出预设范围，体验就会断崖式下跌。

我认为 TERMy 最值得借鉴的不是技术本身，而是它如何通过约束条件倒逼出优雅的解决方案。开发者没有盲目追求“更智能”，而是先问“这个任务真的需要智能吗”。这种思路在 AI 产品设计中很稀缺。未来更务实的路径可能是混合架构：用确定性规则处理 80% 的常见请求，用 LLM 兜底长尾需求，并让系统从 LLM 的成功回答中自动提取新规则。这样既能保持速度和可审计性，又能逐步扩展能力边界。

transferable_methods.name: 约束驱动设计
transferable_methods.principle: 主动限制硬件、数据或响应时间等条件，迫使产品只保留最核心的功能，从而在特定场景下获得极致性能和可靠性。
transferable_methods.applies_when: 适用于资源受限、对延迟或成本敏感、且任务域相对封闭的产品，如嵌入式助手、命令行工具或内部自动化。

transferable_methods.name: 确定性优先的意图路由
transferable_methods.principle: 将用户输入映射到预定义的意图和实体，通过规则引擎直接执行，避免生成式模型的不确定性和高成本。
transferable_methods.applies_when: 适用于用户意图高度集中、命令空间有限、且错误执行代价高的场景，如运维命令、金融交易或医疗设备控制。

product_takeaway: AI 产品经理应该先问“这个任务真的需要生成式模型吗”，而不是默认所有自然语言交互都要用 LLM。确定性规则在速度、成本和可审计性上具有不可替代的优势，混合架构可能是更务实的路径。

NPC-Forge and TERMy development
I love research and development, you may have heard of me because of
PJON (Padded Jittering Operative Network)
. It is a network protocol I started developing in 2010, which was recently
implemented in silicon
by the ETH Zurich university thanks to the research of
I had a chance to focus for 2 months on my personal projects since early July, during the strange times of AI price hikes and the end of subsidized tokenmaxing. I was curious to see if I could develop from scratch a terminal assistant capable of handling simple natural language requests. I have a bad memory and got used to ask to copilot "activate the virtual environment" or similar trivial operations spending a non negligible sum every month. I started thinking, maybe I can do something to make my workflow more efficient? Do I really need trillions of parameters to accomplish those tasks?
Transformers at home
I started an open-ended research on the feasibility of implementing a generative model at home and training it from scratch on the computer I used to play Kerbal Space Program in the early 2010s "upgraded" with 16GB of RAM, NVIDIA GTX 1050 Ti (4GB VRAM) and a i7-4790K (4.0GHz 8 cores) CPU. In my experiments I tend to look for minimalism, so I imposed myself a constrained environment to be forced to work towards an elegant and efficient solution.
I first developed a framework to train and evaluate transformers, which I implemented from scratch in Python. I have started with something very similar to
with 100-200M parameters, then I added flash attention, and all the expected optimizations, I even tried novel architectures like Mamba. The results were generally unsatisfactory, creepy if not outright scary, like the following:
Enter your prompt (or leave blank for empty start): What is an alien? Generating... Using tokenizer: /ollm/checkpoints/gpt/tinyostrich/tokenizer.model === Generated Text === He's not a member of the world. He can't believe anything anymore. All of those animals are looking like excrements, but every mouth is not a bad one. They look alike, all of which are really terrible. They get their own life, and each is a sign that they're not. They're all right, they say. They're just some different things they can make. They've never seen them. They were better not. Some of them've got their rights. Some of them have to go. But we're not looking for the future on how many. The last two of them are all in the universe.
was used instead of an expletive composed of 4 letters that I am not willing to publish in here)
All my tests produced models that were prone to enter in loops repeating the same sentence, and even if trained on QA they were rarely able to consistently answer questions, specially if technical. I trained models on a collection of royalty free books from the
, a lot of open-source software, and various datasets available on
I quickly understood that this approach was not feasible; a proper run would have required at least a month of training non-stop. I was amazed by how my models looked alive and magical, but I was also ashamed because they were incredibly wasteful and effectively useless.
I pivoted to ollama and open-weight models and developed
, yet another terminal harness that uses a pre-prompt to force the model to answer only with terminal commands. Results were generally unsatisfactory because of the time required to get a response. Models like
can get the job done sometimes, but they are not fast and reliable enough for general use, specially if you have only 4GB of VRAM.
Then I remembered about the blockchain craze, when everyone wanted to fit a blockchain somewhere and sell it as the next big thing. I didn't want to waste my time and money like all those people did in the previous hype cycle, so I started building a terminal assistant from scratch with a new set of constraints:

It's kind of antithetical to the tool's deterministic positioning, but have you considered making TERMy leverage an LLM for unseen or low-confidence queries, and then generate the config and update itself to make future similar queries deterministic?
It would make sense to have this integrate with a self-learning routine for an agent: e.g. at night it looks through what it did and writes NPC-Forge recipes. Tomorrow it can answer queries (which he turned added to NPC-Forge) without an LLM. Of course this implies a branching where a query is either processed by NPC-Forge or an LLM, depending on some measure of confidence that NPC-Forge can answer it well.
This is a cool project; I think it's wonderful that traditional NLP methods are being used, rather than reaching straight for an LLM. One significant advantage of not using a local LLM is the significantly simplified dependency stack.
